# What this notebook does

This is a **YAP1C sulfenome pull-down** in *Arabidopsis thaliana*, measured
by data-independent acquisition (DIA) and searched with
[DIA-NN](https://github.com/vdemichev/diann#basics-of-dia-data-analysis).

- **YAP1C** carries a reactive cysteine that forms a mixed disulfide with
  **sulfenylated** (--SOH) cysteines on other proteins, so it traps the
  oxidised interactome.
- **YAP1A** is the matched negative control (the reactive cysteine is
  mutated). Anything it pulls down is sticking to the bait for reasons
  unrelated to sulfenylation, i.e. it is **background**.
- **HL** = high light (oxidative stress), **NL** = normal light (control).

Balanced 2 x 2 design, 4 biological replicates per group, 16 runs:

| Probe (file code) | NL replicates | HL replicates |
|-------------------|---------------|---------------|
| YAP1A (`YA`)      | runs 1--4     | runs 5--8     |
| YAP1C (`YC`)      | runs 13--16   | runs 9--12    |

## The four steps

1.  **Call interactors.** Keep a protein if, in at least one YAP1C
    condition, it was identified in **>= `r params$min_reps` of 4
    replicates** and supported by **>= `r params$min_peptides` peptide(s),
    at least `r params$min_proteotypic` of them unique** to that protein
    group.
2.  **Decide which of those are specific to the active probe**, using two
    independent arguments (the two "Step 2" sections below):
    - **Route A --- absent from YAP1A.** The protein is never seen with a
      unique peptide in any control sample.
    - **Route B --- enriched over YAP1A.** The protein *is* seen in the
      control, but is significantly and substantially more abundant with
      YAP1C (limma, BH-adjusted p < `r params$fdr`, log2FC >
      `r params$log2fc`).
    The **specific interactor set** is the union of the two.
3.  **Ask how high light changes the capture of those proteins**, with two
    complementary tests:
    - **intensity** (limma on log2 MaxLFQ) for proteins quantified in both
      treatments;
    - **detection** (Fisher's exact test on replicate counts) which also
      reaches the on/off proteins that limma cannot test.
    A coverage check then records which arm reached which protein, and
    writes out anything neither arm could test.
4.  **Merge the two tests into one verdict per protein** and draw the
    heatmaps.

## Version note

Compared with the previous version of this notebook:

- The high-light-vs-normal-light comparison now runs on **both** routes to
  specificity (route A **and** route B). Previously it used route A only,
  so every protein that stuck to both probes but stuck much harder to
  YAP1C was dropped before the HL/NL test.
- Duplicated FDR / fold-change / minimum-replicate settings were collapsed
  into one of each (`fdr`, `log2fc`, `min_reps`), so the same rule is
  applied everywhere.
- One heatmap function now serves all four heatmaps; the redundant
  z-scored heatmap and the two "if this package is missing, do something
  else" fallbacks were removed.
- A **test coverage** section now audits both arms protein by protein,
  writes the proteins neither arm could test to their own CSV, and gives
  them a distinct verdict (`not testable`) instead of filing them under
  "no clear difference". Both arms report their coverage split by route, so
  it is visible that the limma-enriched proteins enter both.
- A stacked bar summarises how much of the broadened set is
  treatment-specific, overall and per route.
- A **GO enrichment** section tests the broadened set, and the HL- and
  NL-specific subsets, against the proteins actually detected in this
  experiment, and draws a term-by-list heatmap.

## Glossary

| Term | Plain meaning |
|------|---------------|
| **protein group** | A set of proteins that share the peptides seen, so they cannot be told apart. Written as UniProt accessions joined by `;`. |
| **proteotypic / unique peptide** | A peptide that belongs to only one protein group --- unambiguous evidence. |
| **precursor** | One peptide in one charge state; the thing the mass spectrometer actually measures. |
| **q-value / FDR** | The false-discovery rate. 1% means about 1 in 100 accepted identifications is expected to be wrong. |
| **PG.MaxLFQ** | DIA-NN's protein abundance estimate. Analysed as log2, where +1 means 2-fold higher. |
| **log2FC** | log2 fold-change. 1 = 2-fold up, -1 = 2-fold down. |
| **adjusted p-value** | p-value corrected for testing thousands of proteins (Benjamini-Hochberg). Judge significance on this, not the raw p-value. |
| **limma** | A test that borrows variance information across all proteins, which makes it more reliable than a t-test at n = 4. |
| **NA / grey cell** | Not quantified in that run --- either genuinely absent or below the detection limit. Never treated as zero. |

# Packages

```{r libs}
# Install anything missing, then load. limma comes from Bioconductor.
cran <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "stringr", "readr", "ggplot2", "ggrepel")
gaps <- cran[!vapply(cran, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(gaps)) install.packages(gaps, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

if (!requireNamespace("limma", quietly = TRUE)) {
  if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  BiocManager::install("limma", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(tibble)
  library(stringr); library(readr); library(ggplot2)
})

# report.parquet reader: use arrow if present, otherwise nanoparquet.
read_parquet_any <- function(path) {
  if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE))
    return(as.data.frame(arrow::read_parquet(path)))
  if (!requireNamespace("nanoparquet", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("nanoparquet", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  as.data.frame(nanoparquet::read_parquet(path))
}

# Ensembl Plants connection, used for peptide IDs and for GO terms. Both results
# are cached to disk, so this only runs on the first knit.
plants_mart <- function() {
  if (!requireNamespace("biomaRt", quietly = TRUE)) {
    if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
      install.packages("BiocManager", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
    BiocManager::install("biomaRt", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
  }
  biomaRt::useDataset(dataset = params$mart_dataset,
                      mart    = biomaRt::useMart(biomart = "plants_mart",
                                                 host = params$mart_host))
}

dir.create(params$outdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Sample sheet

```{r design}
# Which raw file is which probe and which light condition.
design <- read_tsv(params$design, show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("Run", "Genotype", "Treatment") %in% names(design)))

design <- design %>%
  mutate(Genotype  = factor(recode(Genotype, YA = "YAP1A", YC = "YAP1C"),
                            levels = c("YAP1A", "YAP1C")),
         Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c("NL", "HL")),
         Group     = paste(Genotype, Treatment, sep = "_")) %>%
  arrange(Genotype, Treatment, Run)     # this order is reused by every heatmap

design
table(design$Genotype, design$Treatment)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# DIA-NN report: load and apply the confidence filters

`report.parquet` is the long precursor-level table: one row per precursor
per run. We keep only target precursors that pass the 1% FDR cut-offs and
carry a positive quantity.

```{r load-report}
rep_raw <- read_parquet_any(params$parquet)
cat("Raw report:", nrow(rep_raw), "rows x", ncol(rep_raw), "columns\n")

stopifnot(all(c("Run", "Protein.Group", "Stripped.Sequence", "Proteotypic",
                "Q.Value", "PG.Q.Value", "PG.MaxLFQ",
                "Precursor.Quantity") %in% names(rep_raw)))

rep <- rep_raw
if ("Decoy" %in% names(rep))          rep <- filter(rep, Decoy == 0)
rep <- filter(rep, Q.Value    <= params$q_value,
                   PG.Q.Value <= params$pg_q_value,
                   Precursor.Quantity > 0)
if ("Global.Q.Value" %in% names(rep)) rep <- filter(rep, Global.Q.Value <= params$global_q)

rep <- inner_join(rep, design, by = "Run")

cat("Confident rows kept:", nrow(rep), "\n")
cat("Runs found:", n_distinct(rep$Run), "of", nrow(design), "\n")
cat("Protein groups:", n_distinct(rep$Protein.Group), "\n")
```

## Identification QC

Each bar is one run. Bars of very different height within a group point to
a weak injection or an unequal pull-down, which is worth knowing before
interpreting any statistics.

```{r qc-ids}
qc <- rep %>%
  group_by(Run, Group) %>%
  summarise(precursors     = n_distinct(Precursor.Id),
            peptides       = n_distinct(Stripped.Sequence),
            protein_groups = n_distinct(Protein.Group), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Group, Run)
qc

ggplot(qc, aes(reorder(Run, protein_groups), protein_groups, fill = Group)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Protein groups (1% FDR)", fill = NULL,
       title = "Protein-group identifications per run") +
  theme_minimal()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# How much evidence supports each protein, in each condition

For every protein group, in each probe x light condition, count: how many
replicates saw it, how many distinct peptides support it, and how many of
those peptides are unique to it.

```{r detection}
evidence <- rep %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Genotype, Treatment) %>%
  summarise(n_reps_detected        = n_distinct(Run),
            n_peptides             = n_distinct(Stripped.Sequence),
            n_proteotypic_peptides = n_distinct(Stripped.Sequence[Proteotypic == 1]),
            .groups = "drop")

# Same information one protein per row, for the exported tables.
evidence_wide <- evidence %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Protein.Group,
              names_from  = c(Genotype, Treatment),
              values_from = c(n_reps_detected, n_peptides, n_proteotypic_peptides),
              values_fill = 0)
head(evidence_wide)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ensembl peptide IDs and protein annotation

Protein groups are keyed by UniProt accession, which is hard to read at the
bench. Here we attach an `ensembl_peptide_id` (AGI-style, e.g.
`AT3G14630.2`) to every group so all lists and figures can be read in
TAIR/Ensembl terms. Where a group carries several accessions
(`A0A1I9LTL1;F4IW82`), each is translated in place and re-joined in the same
order (`AT3G14630.2;AT3G14630.1`).

IDs come from **Ensembl Plants** via **biomaRt** (`athaliana_eg_gene`,
filter `uniprotkb_all`, attribute `ensembl_peptide_id`) and are cached in
`` `r file.path(params$outdir, params$pep_id_cache)` `` so later knits do
not query the server again. If Ensembl is unreachable, or an accession has
no mapped peptide, that position falls back to the UniProt accession --- no
row is ever left blank.

```{r peptide-id-map}
pg_all    <- unique(rep$Protein.Group)
acc_by_pg <- str_split(pg_all, ";")            # accessions per group, order kept
all_acc   <- unique(unlist(acc_by_pg))
all_acc   <- all_acc[nzchar(all_acc)]

cache_path <- file.path(params$outdir, params$pep_id_cache)
if (file.exists(cache_path)) {
  u2p <- read_csv(cache_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  u2p <- tryCatch({
    biomaRt::getBM(attributes = c("uniprotkb_all", "ensembl_peptide_id"),
                   filters    = "uniprotkb_all",
                   values     = all_acc,
                   mart       = plants_mart()) %>%
      filter(nzchar(uniprotkb_all), nzchar(ensembl_peptide_id))
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("!! biomaRt query failed:", conditionMessage(e),
        "\n   peptide IDs will fall back to UniProt accessions.\n")
    tibble(uniprotkb_all = character(), ensembl_peptide_id = character())
  })
  if (nrow(u2p)) write_csv(u2p, cache_path)
}

# One representative peptide ID per accession -> fast lookup table.
lut <- u2p %>%
  filter(nzchar(ensembl_peptide_id)) %>%
  group_by(uniprotkb_all) %>%
  summarise(pep = first(ensembl_peptide_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  { setNames(.$pep, .$uniprotkb_all) }

pg_pep_map <- tibble(
  Protein.Group = pg_all,
  ensembl_peptide_id = vapply(acc_by_pg, function(accs) {
    pep <- unname(lut[accs])
    gap <- is.na(pep) | !nzchar(pep)
    pep[gap] <- accs[gap]                      # fall back to the accession
    paste(pep, collapse = ";")
  }, character(1)))

# pep_label() is used by every figure that needs a readable protein label.
pg2pep    <- setNames(pg_pep_map$ensembl_peptide_id, pg_pep_map$Protein.Group)
pep_label <- function(pg) {
  out <- unname(pg2pep[pg])
  gap <- is.na(out) | !nzchar(out)
  out[gap] <- sub(";.*$", "", pg[gap])         # leading UniProt accession
  out
}

cat(sprintf("Mapped %d/%d accessions; %d/%d protein groups fully mapped.\n",
            sum(all_acc %in% names(lut)), length(all_acc),
            sum(vapply(acc_by_pg, function(a) all(a %in% names(lut)), logical(1))),
            length(pg_all)))
head(pg_pep_map, 10)
```

```{r annotation}
# One annotation row per protein group. This matters: the same group can carry
# slightly different Genes/Protein.Names strings in different runs, and if we
# kept all of them every later join would silently duplicate rows.
annot <- rep %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group) %>%
  summarise(Protein.Ids   = first(Protein.Ids),
            Protein.Names = first(Protein.Names),
            Genes         = first(Genes), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(pg_pep_map, by = "Protein.Group")

if (file.exists(params$prot_desc)) {
  pd <- read_tsv(params$prot_desc, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    group_by(Protein.Id) %>%
    summarise(Description = first(Description), .groups = "drop")
  annot <- annot %>%
    mutate(.first = str_split_fixed(Protein.Ids, ";", 2)[, 1]) %>%
    left_join(pd, by = c(".first" = "Protein.Id")) %>%
    select(-.first)
}

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(annot$Protein.Group))   # guard: exactly one row per group
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 1: call YAP1C interactors

A protein group is an **interactor** if, in at least one YAP1C condition
(NL or HL), it was detected in >= `r params$min_reps`/4 replicates and
supported by >= `r params$min_peptides` distinct peptide(s), of which at
least `r params$min_proteotypic` is unique to the group.

> With the current settings this is the rule *"at least one unique
> peptide, reproducibly in `r params$min_reps` of 4 replicates"*. If you
> want the stricter two-peptide rule, set `min_peptides: 2` in the header
> --- nothing else needs to change.

```{r interactors}
yc_qual <- evidence %>%
  filter(Genotype == "YAP1C") %>%
  mutate(passes = n_reps_detected        >= params$min_reps &
                  n_peptides             >= params$min_peptides &
                  n_proteotypic_peptides >= params$min_proteotypic) %>%
  select(Protein.Group, Treatment, passes) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Treatment, values_from = passes, values_fill = FALSE)

yc_interactors <- yc_qual %>%
  filter(HL | NL) %>%
  mutate(qualifies_in = case_when(HL & NL ~ "both", HL ~ "HL", TRUE ~ "NL"))

cat("YAP1C interactors:", nrow(yc_interactors), "\n")
table(yc_interactors$qualifies_in)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 2, route A: proteins absent from YAP1A

Any protein group with **>= 1 unique peptide in any YAP1A sample** is
called background. This is deliberately strict --- a single unique peptide
in one control run is enough to disqualify a protein --- so route A on its
own is conservative and will discard real targets that also bind the
control weakly. Route B (next section) is what recovers them.

```{r route-a}
ya_background <- rep %>%
  filter(Genotype == "YAP1A", Proteotypic == 1) %>%
  distinct(Protein.Group) %>% pull(Protein.Group)

absent_in_YA <- yc_interactors %>% filter(!Protein.Group %in% ya_background)

cat("YAP1A background groups (>=1 unique peptide in a control run):",
    length(ya_background), "\n")
cat("Route A - interactors absent from YAP1A:", nrow(absent_in_YA), "\n")

write_csv(absent_in_YA %>% left_join(annot, by = "Protein.Group") %>%
            left_join(evidence_wide, by = "Protein.Group") %>% arrange(Genes),
          file.path(params$outdir, "unique_YAP1C_interactors.csv"))
write_csv(tibble(Protein.Group = ya_background) %>% left_join(annot, by = "Protein.Group"),
          file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1A_background_list.csv"))
write_csv(yc_interactors %>% left_join(annot, by = "Protein.Group"),
          file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_all_interactors.csv"))

tibble(step = c("Protein groups in the filtered report",
                "YAP1C interactors",
                "of which also in YAP1A background",
                "Route A: absent from YAP1A"),
       n = c(n_distinct(rep$Protein.Group),
             nrow(yc_interactors),
             sum(yc_interactors$Protein.Group %in% ya_background),
             nrow(absent_in_YA)))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 2, route B: proteins enriched in YAP1C over YAP1A

Here we keep the proteins route A throws away, and ask a quantitative
question instead: *is this protein pulled down substantially more by the
active probe than by the control?*

**Intensity table.** One log2 `PG.MaxLFQ` value per protein per run, all 16
samples. (MaxLFQ is constant across the precursors of a group within a run,
so one value per Run x Protein.Group defines the matrix.)

```{r matrix-all}
pg_long <- rep %>%
  distinct(Run, Protein.Group, PG.MaxLFQ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(PG.MaxLFQ), PG.MaxLFQ > 0)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pg_long[c("Run", "Protein.Group")]))   # one value per cell

log2_all <- pg_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Run, values_from = PG.MaxLFQ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Protein.Group") %>%
  as.matrix() %>% log2()
# columns in a fixed, readable order: YAP1A NL, YAP1A HL, YAP1C NL, YAP1C HL
log2_all <- log2_all[, design$Run[design$Run %in% colnames(log2_all)], drop = FALSE]

meta <- design %>% filter(Run %in% colnames(log2_all)) %>%
  arrange(match(Run, colnames(log2_all)))

cat("Full matrix:", nrow(log2_all), "proteins x", ncol(log2_all), "runs",
    sprintf("(%d YAP1A, %d YAP1C)\n",
            sum(meta$Genotype == "YAP1A"), sum(meta$Genotype == "YAP1C")))
```

```{r heatmap-helper}
# One function draws every heatmap in this notebook.
#   pg    : protein groups to show, first one at the top
#   mat   : log2 intensity matrix (log2_all = 16 samples, log2mat = 8 YAP1C samples)
#   facet : how to split the columns ("Treatment", or "Genotype + Treatment")
# Missing values stay grey - they are never filled in for plotting.
lfq_heatmap <- function(pg, mat, facet = "Treatment", title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                        max_rows_labelled = 80) {
  pg <- unique(pg[pg %in% rownames(mat)])
  if (!length(pg)) { cat("Nothing to plot for:", title, "\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  # optional = TRUE keeps the run names exactly as they are in the matrix
  df <- as.data.frame(mat[pg, , drop = FALSE], optional = TRUE) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Protein.Group") %>%
    pivot_longer(-Protein.Group, names_to = "Run", values_to = "log2LFQ") %>%
    left_join(select(design, Run, Genotype, Treatment), by = "Run") %>%
    mutate(Run = factor(Run, levels = colnames(mat)),
           Protein.Group = factor(Protein.Group, levels = rev(pg)))
  ggplot(df, aes(Run, Protein.Group, fill = log2LFQ)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "grey92") +
    facet_grid(as.formula(paste(". ~", facet)), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C", na.value = "grey88",
                         name = "log2 LFQ\n(PG.MaxLFQ)") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = setNames(pep_label(pg), pg)) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y  = if (length(pg) <= max_rows_labelled) element_text(size = 6)
                         else element_blank(),
          panel.grid   = element_blank(),
          strip.text   = element_text(size = 8))
}

# Sort protein groups by how much stronger they are in HL than in NL, biggest first.
order_by_hl_minus_nl <- function(pg, mat, hl_runs, nl_runs) {
  pg <- unique(pg[pg %in% rownames(mat)])
  d  <- rowMeans(mat[pg, hl_runs, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) -
        rowMeans(mat[pg, nl_runs, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  pg[order(d, decreasing = TRUE, na.last = TRUE)]
}

# Sort by mean log2 LFQ across only the runs where the protein was detected
# (na.rm drops the blanks), most abundant first. Use this rather than HL - NL
# whenever a set contains treatment-exclusive proteins: one of their two means
# is taken over nothing at all, so the difference is undefined and they would
# otherwise be dumped at the bottom of the plot in arbitrary order.
order_by_mean_lfq <- function(pg, mat) {
  pg <- unique(pg[pg %in% rownames(mat)])
  if (!length(pg)) return(pg)
  m <- rowMeans(mat[pg, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  pg[order(m, decreasing = TRUE, na.last = TRUE)]
}
```

**Missing values.** The 16 samples form four groups of four replicates
(YAP1A_NL, YAP1A_HL, YAP1C_NL, YAP1C_HL). Within a group, a protein counts
as **valid** if it was quantified in >= `r params$min_reps` of the 4
replicates; missing cells in a valid group are filled with the mean of the
replicates that *were* observed. Groups that fail the
`r params$min_reps`/4 rule are left empty and are **not** invented ---
limma simply ignores those samples for that protein.

```{r route-b-prep}
# Which columns belong to each of the four replicate groups.
group_cols <- split(seq_len(nrow(meta)), meta$Group)

# valid[protein, group] = TRUE if that group observed the protein >= min_reps times.
valid <- sapply(group_cols, function(cols)
  rowSums(!is.na(log2_all[, cols, drop = FALSE])) >= params$min_reps)

# Fill the gaps inside valid groups with that group's observed mean.
Xe <- log2_all
for (g in colnames(valid)) {
  cols <- group_cols[[g]]
  gmean <- rowMeans(log2_all[, cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  for (j in cols) {
    hole <- is.na(Xe[, j]) & valid[, g]
    Xe[hole, j] <- gmean[hole]
  }
}

# Only proteins seen properly in BOTH probes can be compared between probes.
seen_in_YA <- rowSums(valid[, grep("^YAP1A", colnames(valid)), drop = FALSE]) > 0
seen_in_YC <- rowSums(valid[, grep("^YAP1C", colnames(valid)), drop = FALSE]) > 0
Xe <- Xe[seen_in_YA & seen_in_YC, , drop = FALSE]

cat("Proteins testable for YAP1C vs YAP1A (valid in >=", params$min_reps,
    "/4 of a group in both probes):", nrow(Xe), "\n")
```

**The test.** limma with the design `~ 0 + Genotype` and the contrast
**YAP1C - YAP1A**; variance is stabilised across proteins with empirical
Bayes and p-values corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg. Light condition is
pooled here, since the question is about the probe, not the light (to model
light as well, use `~ 0 + Genotype + Treatment`). Proteins with adjusted p <
`r params$fdr` **and** log2FC > `r params$log2fc` are the route B set.

```{r route-b-test}
des_g <- model.matrix(~ 0 + Genotype, data = meta)
fit   <- limma::lmFit(Xe, des_g)
fit   <- limma::contrasts.fit(
  fit, limma::makeContrasts(GenotypeYAP1C - GenotypeYAP1A, levels = des_g))
fit   <- limma::eBayes(fit)

enr <- limma::topTable(fit, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") %>%
  rownames_to_column("Protein.Group") %>%
  transmute(Protein.Group, log2FC_YC_vs_YA = logFC, AveExpr, t,
            pvalue = P.Value, adj_pvalue = adj.P.Val) %>%
  mutate(class = case_when(
    adj_pvalue < params$fdr & log2FC_YC_vs_YA >  params$log2fc ~ "enriched in YAP1C",
    adj_pvalue < params$fdr & log2FC_YC_vs_YA <  0             ~ "enriched in YAP1A",
    TRUE                                                       ~ "ns")) %>%
  arrange(adj_pvalue)

enriched_in_YC <- filter(enr, class == "enriched in YAP1C")

write_csv(enr %>% left_join(annot, by = "Protein.Group"),
          file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_vs_YAP1A_limma.csv"))
write_csv(enriched_in_YC %>% left_join(annot, by = "Protein.Group"),
          file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_enriched_significant.csv"))

cat(sprintf("Route B - enriched in YAP1C (adj.p < %.2g & log2FC > %g): %d\n",
            params$fdr, params$log2fc, nrow(enriched_in_YC)))
enriched_in_YC %>%
  transmute(uniprot = Protein.Group, peptide_id = pep_label(Protein.Group),
            log2FC_YC_vs_YA, adj_pvalue) %>% head(25)
```

## Volcano: YAP1C vs YAP1A

```{r route-b-volcano, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
ggplot(enr, aes(log2FC_YC_vs_YA, -log10(pvalue), colour = class)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = params$log2fc, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = head(enriched_in_YC, 25),
                           aes(label = pep_label(Protein.Group)),
                           size = 3, max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("enriched in YAP1C" = "#c0392b",
                                 "enriched in YAP1A" = "#2471a3",
                                 "ns" = "grey75")) +
  labs(title = "YAP1C vs YAP1A (limma, both light conditions pooled)",
       subtitle = sprintf("route B set: adj.p < %.2g & log2FC > %g",
                          params$fdr, params$log2fc),
       x = "log2 fold-change (YAP1C / YAP1A)", y = "-log10 p-value", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## The strongest route B proteins across all 16 samples

Both contrasts read at once: **YAP1C vs YAP1A** across the probe panels,
**NL vs HL** within each probe.

```{r route-b-heatmap, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
top_enriched <- head(enriched_in_YC$Protein.Group[
  order(enriched_in_YC$log2FC_YC_vs_YA, decreasing = TRUE)], 60)

lfq_heatmap(top_enriched, mat = log2_all, facet = "Genotype + Treatment",
            title = "Top route B proteins (enriched in YAP1C) - log2 LFQ",
            subtitle = "up to 60 proteins, strongest enrichment at the top; grey = not quantified")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 2, combined: the specific interactor set carried forward

The two routes answer the same question with different evidence, so we take
their **union**. Note that they are nearly non-overlapping *by
construction*: route A requires a protein to be absent from YAP1A, while
route B requires it to be quantified in YAP1A. The small `both routes`
overlap is made up of proteins detected in the control **only via shared
(non-unique) peptides** --- enough to be quantified, not enough to count as
background.

**This union is the set used by every HL-vs-NL analysis below.**

```{r specific-set}
specific <- annot %>%
  filter(Protein.Group %in% union(absent_in_YA$Protein.Group,
                                  enriched_in_YC$Protein.Group)) %>%
  mutate(in_A = Protein.Group %in% absent_in_YA$Protein.Group,
         in_B = Protein.Group %in% enriched_in_YC$Protein.Group,
         route = case_when(in_A & in_B ~ "both routes",
                           in_A        ~ "A: absent from YAP1A",
                           TRUE        ~ "B: enriched over YAP1A")) %>%
  select(-in_A, -in_B) %>%
  left_join(select(yc_interactors, Protein.Group, qualifies_in), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  # Route B proteins were selected on abundance alone; this flags whether they
  # also clear the step-1 evidence bar (>= min_reps replicates + unique peptide).
  mutate(passes_step1 = !is.na(qualifies_in))

if (!isTRUE(params$include_enriched))
  specific <- filter(specific, route != "B: enriched over YAP1A")

write_csv(specific, file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_specific_interactors_broadened.csv"))

cat("Specific interactors carried into the HL vs NL analysis:", nrow(specific), "\n")
print(table(specific$route))
cat("\nOf these, how many also pass the step-1 evidence rule:\n")
print(table(route = specific$route, passes_step1 = specific$passes_step1))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Intensity table for the YAP1C samples

The eight YAP1C runs, restricted to the specific interactors. This is a
straight subset of the 16-sample matrix built above, so the two halves of
the notebook cannot drift apart.

```{r matrix-yc}
yc_meta <- filter(meta, Genotype == "YAP1C")
yc_runs <- yc_meta$Run                                   # NL block, then HL block
hl_runs <- yc_meta$Run[yc_meta$Treatment == "HL"]
nl_runs <- yc_meta$Run[yc_meta$Treatment == "NL"]

log2mat <- log2_all[intersect(specific$Protein.Group, rownames(log2_all)), yc_runs,
                    drop = FALSE]
log2mat <- log2mat[rowSums(!is.na(log2mat)) > 0, , drop = FALSE]

cat("HL vs NL matrix:", nrow(log2mat), "proteins x", ncol(log2mat), "YAP1C runs\n")
cat("Specific interactors with no MaxLFQ value in any YAP1C run (not plottable):",
    nrow(specific) - nrow(log2mat), "\n")
```

```{r pca, fig.height=4}
# Sanity check: do the replicates separate by light condition?
ok <- log2mat[rowSums(is.na(log2mat)) == 0, , drop = FALSE]
ok <- ok[rowSums((ok - rowMeans(ok))^2) > 0, , drop = FALSE]   # drop flat rows
if (nrow(ok) > 2) {
  pca <- prcomp(t(ok), scale. = TRUE)
  ve  <- round(100 * summary(pca)$importance[2, 1:2])
  as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2]) %>% rownames_to_column("Run") %>%
    left_join(select(design, Run, Treatment), by = "Run") %>%
    ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = Treatment, label = Run)) +
      geom_point(size = 3) +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
      labs(title = "PCA of the YAP1C samples",
           subtitle = sprintf("%d proteins quantified in all 8 runs", nrow(ok)),
           x = paste0("PC1 (", ve[1], "%)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", ve[2], "%)")) +
      theme_minimal()
} else cat("Too few complete-case proteins for a PCA.\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 3, arm 1: HL vs NL by intensity (limma)

This arm asks *"is the protein captured more strongly?"*, so it needs
numbers in both treatments: we test only proteins with >= `r params$min_reps`
quantified values **in each** YAP1C group. Proteins present in essentially
one treatment cannot be tested here --- they are picked up by arm 2, so
nothing is quietly lost.

```{r hl-vs-nl-quant-prep}
n_HL <- rowSums(!is.na(log2mat[, hl_runs, drop = FALSE]))
n_NL <- rowSums(!is.na(log2mat[, nl_runs, drop = FALSE]))
X <- log2mat[n_HL >= params$min_reps & n_NL >= params$min_reps, , drop = FALSE]

# Fill the few remaining gaps with that treatment's observed mean (every row
# here already has at least min_reps real values per treatment).
for (cols in list(hl_runs, nl_runs)) {
  m <- rowMeans(X[, cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  for (j in cols) { hole <- is.na(X[, j]); X[hole, j] <- m[hole] }
}

cat("Testable by intensity:", nrow(X), "of", nrow(log2mat), "specific interactors\n")
# Broken down by how each protein earned its place in the specific set, so it is
# visible that route B (limma-enriched) proteins enter this arm too.
print(table(route  = specific$route[match(rownames(log2mat), specific$Protein.Group)],
            fitted = ifelse(rownames(log2mat) %in% rownames(X), "yes", "no")))
```

```{r hl-vs-nl-quant-test}
trt <- yc_meta$Treatment[match(colnames(X), yc_meta$Run)]   # NL / HL, one per column
des <- model.matrix(~ 0 + trt)
colnames(des) <- sub("^trt", "", colnames(des))             # -> "NL", "HL"

fit <- limma::lmFit(X, des)
fit <- limma::contrasts.fit(fit, limma::makeContrasts(HL - NL, levels = des))
fit <- limma::eBayes(fit)

de <- limma::topTable(fit, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") %>%
  rownames_to_column("Protein.Group") %>%
  transmute(Protein.Group, log2FC_HL_vs_NL = logFC, AveExpr, t,
            pvalue = P.Value, adj_pvalue = adj.P.Val) %>%
  mutate(direction = case_when(
    adj_pvalue < params$fdr & log2FC_HL_vs_NL >=  params$log2fc ~ "up in HL",
    adj_pvalue < params$fdr & log2FC_HL_vs_NL <= -params$log2fc ~ "down in HL",
    TRUE                                                        ~ "ns")) %>%
  arrange(adj_pvalue)

write_csv(de %>% left_join(specific, by = "Protein.Group"),
          file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_differential.csv"))

cat(sprintf("Significant (adj.p < %.2g & |log2FC| >= %g): %d  (up in HL = %d, down = %d)\n",
            params$fdr, params$log2fc, sum(de$direction != "ns"),
            sum(de$direction == "up in HL"), sum(de$direction == "down in HL")))
de %>% left_join(select(specific, Protein.Group, Genes, route), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  head(20)
```

## Volcano: HL vs NL

```{r hl-vs-nl-volcano, fig.height=6}
sig_line <- if (any(de$direction != "ns"))
  -log10(max(de$pvalue[de$direction != "ns"], na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_

ggplot(de, aes(log2FC_HL_vs_NL, -log10(pvalue), colour = direction)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1) * params$log2fc, linetype = "dashed") +
  { if (!is.na(sig_line))
      geom_hline(yintercept = sig_line, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") } +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(de, direction != "ns"),
                           aes(label = pep_label(Protein.Group)),
                           size = 3, max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("up in HL" = "#c0392b",
                                 "down in HL" = "#2471a3", "ns" = "grey70")) +
  labs(title = "High light vs normal light - specific YAP1C interactors",
       subtitle = "dashed horizontal line = the significance threshold actually reached",
       x = "log2 fold-change (HL / NL)", y = "-log10 p-value", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 3, arm 2: HL vs NL by detection (Fisher's exact test)

Covalent trapping by YAP1C behaves more like an **on/off** event near the
detection limit than a graded fold-change, and in this kind of experiment
the proteins that respond to high light are largely **gained or lost**
rather than scaled up or down --- exactly the proteins arm 1 cannot test.
So this arm ignores intensity and tests **detection**: for each specific
interactor, count how many of the 4 HL and 4 NL replicates identified it,
and apply Fisher's exact test to the 2 x 2 table.

Two descriptive labels come out of the same counts:

- **`detection_class`** --- the raw on/off picture: `HL-only`, `NL-only`
  (seen at least once in one treatment, never in the other) or `shared`.
- **`pattern`** --- how *reproducible* that is, using the
  `r params$min_reps`/4 rule: `HL-exclusive`, `NL-exclusive` (reproducible
  in one treatment, absent from the other), `HL-biased`, `NL-biased`
  (reproducible in one, patchy in the other), `both treatments`, or
  `sparse` (never reproducible anywhere).

```{r hl-vs-nl-detection}
n_rep_HL <- length(hl_runs); n_rep_NL <- length(nl_runs)

det_counts <- rep %>%
  filter(Genotype == "YAP1C", Protein.Group %in% specific$Protein.Group) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Treatment) %>%
  summarise(n_det = n_distinct(Run), .groups = "drop")

pa <- specific %>% select(Protein.Group) %>%
  left_join(det_counts %>% filter(Treatment == "HL") %>%
              transmute(Protein.Group, det_HL = n_det), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  left_join(det_counts %>% filter(Treatment == "NL") %>%
              transmute(Protein.Group, det_NL = n_det), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(det_HL = replace_na(det_HL, 0L), det_NL = replace_na(det_NL, 0L),
         detection_class = case_when(det_HL > 0 & det_NL == 0 ~ "HL-only",
                                     det_NL > 0 & det_HL == 0 ~ "NL-only",
                                     TRUE                     ~ "shared"),
         pattern = case_when(
           det_HL >= params$min_reps & det_NL == 0               ~ "HL-exclusive",
           det_NL >= params$min_reps & det_HL == 0               ~ "NL-exclusive",
           det_HL >= params$min_reps & det_NL <  params$min_reps ~ "HL-biased",
           det_NL >= params$min_reps & det_HL <  params$min_reps ~ "NL-biased",
           det_HL >= params$min_reps & det_NL >= params$min_reps ~ "both treatments",
           TRUE                                                  ~ "sparse"),
         # the coarse grouping used by the specificity bar chart and the GO analysis
         specificity = case_when(
           pattern %in% c("HL-exclusive", "HL-biased") ~ "HL-specific",
           pattern %in% c("NL-exclusive", "NL-biased") ~ "NL-specific",
           pattern == "both treatments"                ~ "both treatments",
           TRUE                                        ~ "sparse"),
         fisher_p = mapply(function(a, b)
           fisher.test(matrix(c(a, n_rep_HL - a, b, n_rep_NL - b), nrow = 2))$p.value,
           det_HL, det_NL),
         fisher_adj = p.adjust(fisher_p, "BH"),
         pa_direction = case_when(
           fisher_adj < params$fdr & det_HL > det_NL ~ "more in HL",
           fisher_adj < params$fdr & det_NL > det_HL ~ "more in NL",
           TRUE                                      ~ "ns"),
         tested_by_intensity = Protein.Group %in% rownames(X)) %>%
  arrange(fisher_p, desc(abs(det_HL - det_NL)))

write_csv(pa %>% left_join(specific, by = "Protein.Group"),
          file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_presence_absence.csv"))
write_csv(pa %>% filter(!tested_by_intensity) %>% left_join(specific, by = "Protein.Group"),
          file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_condition_exclusive.csv"))

cat("Detection pattern by route into the specific set:\n")
print(table(route   = specific$route[match(pa$Protein.Group, specific$Protein.Group)],
            pattern = pa$pattern))
cat(sprintf("\nFisher test significant (adj.p < %.2g): %d  (more in HL = %d, more in NL = %d)\n",
            params$fdr, sum(pa$pa_direction != "ns"),
            sum(pa$pa_direction == "more in HL"), sum(pa$pa_direction == "more in NL")))
pa %>% left_join(select(specific, Protein.Group, Genes, route), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  head(20)
```

> **How much can this test see?** With 4 versus 4 replicates the most
> extreme table possible (4 vs 0) gives a two-sided Fisher p of about
> 0.029. A perfectly clean on/off protein is therefore only just
> significant before correction, and may well not survive BH adjustment
> across thousands of proteins. Read `fisher_adj` as a **ranking of on/off
> evidence** alongside the raw `det_HL` and `det_NL` counts, not as a
> yes/no answer.

## Detection landscape

```{r detection-landscape, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(pa, aes(det_NL, det_HL)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_count(aes(colour = detection_class), alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:n_rep_NL) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:n_rep_HL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("HL-only" = "#c0392b",
                                 "NL-only" = "#2471a3", "shared" = "#7f8c8d")) +
  labs(title = "Detection landscape of the specific YAP1C interactors",
       subtitle = "points off the diagonal are treatment-biased in detection",
       x = sprintf("# NL replicates detected (of %d)", n_rep_NL),
       y = sprintf("# HL replicates detected (of %d)", n_rep_HL),
       size = "# proteins", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Are they treatment-specific?

The same detection patterns, counted rather than plotted per protein. The
bars split the broadened set into proteins reproducibly captured in **one**
light condition only (treatment-specific, red for HL and blue for NL) and
proteins captured in **both** (grey). Bars are also shown per route, so you
can see whether the two definitions of specificity behave the same way.

```{r treatment-specificity-bar, fig.height=4.5}
# Classes come straight from the arm 2 detection patterns, so this figure and
# the tables above cannot disagree.
spec_levels <- c("HL-exclusive", "HL-biased", "both treatments",
                 "NL-biased", "NL-exclusive", "sparse")
spec_cols <- c("HL-exclusive" = "#c0392b", "HL-biased"    = "#d98880",
               "both treatments" = "#7f8c8d",
               "NL-biased"    = "#7fb3d5", "NL-exclusive" = "#2471a3",
               "sparse"       = "#d5dbdb")

ts <- pa %>%
  select(Protein.Group, pattern, specificity) %>%
  left_join(select(specific, Protein.Group, route), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(pattern = factor(pattern, levels = spec_levels),
         treatment_specific = specificity %in% c("HL-specific", "NL-specific"))

# one bar per route, plus an "all interactors" bar for the set as a whole
all_label  <- "All specific\ninteractors"
ts_counts  <- bind_rows(mutate(ts, group = all_label), mutate(ts, group = route)) %>%
  group_by(group, pattern) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c(all_label, sort(unique(ts$route)))),
         # dark fills need white numbers, light fills need dark ones
         label_colour = ifelse(pattern %in% c("HL-biased", "NL-biased", "sparse"),
                               "grey15", "white"))

ggplot(ts_counts, aes(group, n, fill = pattern)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n, colour = label_colour), size = 3,
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = spec_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  labs(title = "Are the specific YAP1C interactors treatment-specific?",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d of %d (%.0f%%) are reproducible in one light condition only (>= %d/4 there)",
                          sum(ts$treatment_specific), nrow(ts),
                          100 * mean(ts$treatment_specific), params$min_reps),
       x = NULL, y = "protein groups") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

# the numbers behind the figure
ts %>% group_by(route) %>%
  summarise(n_interactors        = n(),
            n_treatment_specific = sum(treatment_specific),
            percent_specific     = round(100 * n_treatment_specific / n_interactors, 1),
            .groups = "drop")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Test coverage: which arm reached which protein

Before reading any verdict it is worth knowing which proteins each arm could
actually say something about, because the two arms have **different entry
requirements** and use slightly different evidence:

- **Arm 1 (intensity)** needs a MaxLFQ *number* in >= `r params$min_reps` of
  the 4 replicates of **each** treatment. A protein quantified in only one
  treatment cannot be fitted, and one identified but never quantified is
  invisible to this arm (and to every heatmap) altogether.
- **Arm 2 (detection)** only needs replicate *identification* counts, so it
  reaches almost everything. Identification and quantification are not the
  same thing --- a run can identify a protein and still report no MaxLFQ
  value --- which is a common reason for dropping out of arm 1 while staying
  in arm 2.

`tested_in` therefore takes four values: `both arms`, `intensity only`,
`detection only`, and `neither`. A protein counts as tested by arm 2 if its
2 x 2 table contains at least one YAP1C identification; where HL and NL
counts are **equal** the test still runs and returns p = 1, which is a real
answer ("no detection difference"), not a failure --- the
`detection_informative` column flags those so they are not over-read.
`neither` means no result came out of either arm, and those proteins are
written to their own CSV with the reason spelled out. Given how the
specific set is built this should be empty; the code checks rather than
assumes.

```{r coverage-check}
# n_HL / n_NL are the arm 1 inputs: how many YAP1C runs carry a MaxLFQ number.
quant_counts <- tibble(Protein.Group = rownames(log2mat),
                       n_quant_HL = unname(n_HL), n_quant_NL = unname(n_NL))

coverage <- specific %>%
  select(Protein.Group, ensembl_peptide_id, Genes, Protein.Names,
         any_of("Description"), route, qualifies_in, passes_step1) %>%
  left_join(quant_counts, by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  left_join(select(pa, Protein.Group, det_HL, det_NL, pattern, fisher_p),
            by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  left_join(select(de, Protein.Group, adj_pvalue), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(
    n_quant_HL = replace_na(n_quant_HL, 0),
    n_quant_NL = replace_na(n_quant_NL, 0),
    in_quant_matrix = Protein.Group %in% rownames(log2mat),
    tested_by_intensity = !is.na(adj_pvalue),                      # limma fitted it
    tested_by_detection = !is.na(fisher_p) & (det_HL + det_NL) > 0,# a non-empty 2x2 table
    # equal HL and NL counts give p = 1 whatever the biology, so flag them
    detection_informative = tested_by_detection & det_HL != det_NL,
    tested_in = case_when(
      tested_by_intensity & tested_by_detection ~ "both arms",
      tested_by_intensity                       ~ "intensity only",
      tested_by_detection                       ~ "detection only",
      TRUE                                      ~ "neither"),
    why_not_tested = case_when(
      tested_in != "neither"                  ~ NA_character_,
      is.na(det_HL) | is.na(det_NL)           ~ "no detection counts - unexpected, check the report",
      det_HL + det_NL == 0 & !in_quant_matrix ~ "never identified and never quantified in any YAP1C run",
      det_HL + det_NL == 0                    ~ "never identified in any YAP1C run",
      TRUE                                    ~ "not fitted by arm 1 and no usable detection table")) %>%
  select(-adj_pvalue, -fisher_p) %>%
  arrange(factor(tested_in, levels = c("neither", "detection only",
                                       "intensity only", "both arms")), Genes)

write_csv(coverage, file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_test_coverage.csv"))

untested <- filter(coverage, tested_in == "neither")
write_csv(untested, file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_untested.csv"))

cat("Coverage of the", nrow(coverage), "specific interactors, by route:\n")
print(table(route = coverage$route, tested_in = coverage$tested_in))

cat("\nTested by NEITHER arm:", nrow(untested), "\n")
cat("Not fitted by arm 1, so relying on the detection answer alone:",
    sum(!coverage$tested_by_intensity), "\n")
cat("Identified but never quantified (invisible to arm 1 and to every heatmap):",
    sum(!coverage$in_quant_matrix), "\n")
cat("Equal HL and NL detection counts, so arm 2 can only return p = 1:",
    sum(coverage$det_HL == coverage$det_NL, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

if (nrow(untested)) {
  print(table(untested$why_not_tested))
  untested %>% select(Protein.Group, Genes, route, n_quant_HL, n_quant_NL,
                      det_HL, det_NL, why_not_tested) %>% head(30)
} else {
  cat("\n-> every specific interactor was reached by at least one arm.",
      "\n   YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_untested.csv is written with headers and no rows.\n")
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 4: one verdict per protein

Each specific interactor gets a single answer: the **intensity** result
where the protein was testable in both treatments, otherwise the
**detection** result. Two columns keep the reading honest: `route` records
how the protein earned its place in the specific set, so you can check
whether the two routes tell the same story, and `tested_in` records which
arm could reach it. Proteins neither arm could test are labelled
**`not testable (no HL/NL information)`** rather than
`no clear NL/HL difference` --- an absence of evidence, not evidence of
absence.

```{r combined-verdict}
verdict_levels <- c("HL-enriched (quant)", "HL-gained (presence)", "HL-leaning (detection)",
                    "NL-enriched (quant)", "NL-gained (presence)", "NL-leaning (detection)",
                    "no clear NL/HL difference", "not testable (no HL/NL information)")

combined <- specific %>%
  select(Protein.Group, ensembl_peptide_id, Genes, Protein.Names,
         any_of("Description"), route, qualifies_in) %>%
  left_join(select(coverage, Protein.Group, tested_in, in_quant_matrix,
                   n_quant_HL, n_quant_NL), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  left_join(select(pa, Protein.Group, det_HL, det_NL, detection_class, pattern,
                   fisher_p, fisher_adj, pa_direction), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  left_join(select(de, Protein.Group, log2FC_HL_vs_NL, pvalue, adj_pvalue, direction),
            by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(tested_by_intensity = !is.na(adj_pvalue),
         verdict = case_when(
           tested_by_intensity & direction == "up in HL"   ~ "HL-enriched (quant)",
           tested_by_intensity & direction == "down in HL" ~ "NL-enriched (quant)",
           pa_direction == "more in HL"                    ~ "HL-gained (presence)",
           pa_direction == "more in NL"                    ~ "NL-gained (presence)",
           detection_class == "HL-only"                    ~ "HL-leaning (detection)",
           detection_class == "NL-only"                    ~ "NL-leaning (detection)",
           # separated from the line below on purpose: "no test was possible" is
           # not the same statement as "we tested and found no difference"
           tested_in == "neither"       ~ "not testable (no HL/NL information)",
           TRUE                         ~ "no clear NL/HL difference")) %>%
  arrange(factor(verdict, levels = verdict_levels), coalesce(adj_pvalue, fisher_adj))

write_csv(combined, file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_combined_verdict.csv"))

cat("Verdict by route into the specific set:\n")
print(table(verdict = factor(combined$verdict, levels = verdict_levels),
            route   = combined$route))
combined %>% filter(!verdict %in% c("no clear NL/HL difference",
                                    "not testable (no HL/NL information)")) %>% head(30)
```

# Heatmaps

All three heatmaps show **absolute log2 PG.MaxLFQ** (not z-scored) across
the eight YAP1C runs, NL block beside HL block, so intensities can be
compared directly. Cells that were never quantified stay **grey**, which is
what makes on/off behaviour visible.

## Condition-biased interactors

Reproducible (>= `r params$min_reps`/4) in one treatment but not the other.

```{r heatmap-biased, fig.height=7}
biased <- filter(pa, pattern %in% c("HL-exclusive", "NL-exclusive",
                                    "HL-biased", "NL-biased"))
cat("Condition-biased interactors:", nrow(biased), "\n"); print(table(biased$pattern))

lfq_heatmap(order_by_mean_lfq(biased$Protein.Group, log2mat),
            mat = log2mat,
            title = "Condition-biased specific interactors - log2 LFQ",
            subtitle = sprintf(">= %d/4 replicates in one treatment only; rows ordered by mean log2 LFQ where detected, highest at the top; grey = not quantified",
                               params$min_reps))
```

## Treatment-exclusive interactors

The strict on/off cases: reproducible in one treatment, **never** seen in
the other. One block is entirely grey by construction, so rows are grouped
by class and ordered by mean intensity rather than by HL - NL.

```{r heatmap-exclusive, fig.height=6}
exclusive <- filter(pa, pattern %in% c("HL-exclusive", "NL-exclusive"))
cat("Treatment-exclusive interactors:", nrow(exclusive), "\n")
print(table(exclusive$pattern))

# Each class kept as a block, and within a block the most abundant first.
ex_pg <- c(order_by_mean_lfq(exclusive$Protein.Group[exclusive$pattern == "HL-exclusive"],
                             log2mat),
           order_by_mean_lfq(exclusive$Protein.Group[exclusive$pattern == "NL-exclusive"],
                             log2mat))

lfq_heatmap(ex_pg, mat = log2mat,
            title = "Treatment-exclusive specific interactors - log2 LFQ",
            subtitle = sprintf(">= %d/4 in one treatment, 0/4 in the other; HL-exclusive block on top",
                               params$min_reps))
```

## Every specific interactor

```{r heatmap-all, fig.height=11}
lfq_heatmap(order_by_hl_minus_nl(rownames(log2mat), log2mat, hl_runs, nl_runs),
            mat = log2mat,
            title = "All specific YAP1C interactors - log2 LFQ, NL vs HL",
            subtitle = "rows ordered by HL - NL mean log2 LFQ; grey = not quantified")
```

# GO term enrichment

Which biological functions are over-represented among the specific YAP1C
interactors --- and do the HL-specific and NL-specific proteins do
different jobs?

**The background matters more than the test.** The comparison set here is
**every protein group identified in this experiment**, not every gene in
the genome. A pull-down only sees abundant, extractable, MS-friendly
proteins, so testing against the whole genome mostly rediscovers that fact
and returns "ribosome", "chloroplast", "cytosol" no matter what the bait
was. Against the detected background, a term is only enriched if it stands
out among proteins the experiment could have seen.

Annotations come from **`org.At.tair.db`**, the Bioconductor annotation
package for Arabidopsis. It is keyed on TAIR loci, which is exactly what the
protein groups map to, and it works offline once installed --- no web service
to time out mid-knit. One locus is used per protein group (the first mapped
accession). Annotations are then **propagated up the GO hierarchy** with
`GO.db`: a protein annotated to *response to hydrogen peroxide* is by
definition also annotated to *response to oxidative stress*, and without
propagation those broader categories would be badly under-counted.

```{r go-annotation}
# GO annotations come from org.At.tair.db, the Bioconductor annotation package
# for Arabidopsis. It is keyed on TAIR loci - exactly what the protein groups
# map to - and works offline once installed, so there is no web service to fail.
for (pkg in c("GO.db", "org.At.tair.db")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
      install.packages("BiocManager", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
    BiocManager::install(pkg, update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
  }
}

# --- 1. protein group -> TAIR locus --------------------------------------
# AT3G14630.2 -> AT3G14630. Groups whose ID fell back to a UniProt accession
# have no locus and drop out here.
pg2gene <- annot %>%
  transmute(Protein.Group,
            gene = toupper(sub("\\.\\d+$", "", sub(";.*$", "", ensembl_peptide_id)))) %>%
  filter(grepl("^AT[1-5CM]G[0-9]{5}$", gene))

cat(sprintf("Protein groups with a TAIR locus: %d of %d\n",
            nrow(pg2gene), nrow(annot)))

# --- 2. TAIR locus -> GO term --------------------------------------------
# Only ask about loci the package recognises: select() errors outright if none
# of the keys are valid, and warns confusingly if some are not.
known_keys <- AnnotationDbi::keys(org.At.tair.db::org.At.tair.db, keytype = "TAIR")
go_keys    <- intersect(unique(pg2gene$gene), known_keys)

g2go <- if (length(go_keys)) {
  suppressMessages(
    AnnotationDbi::select(org.At.tair.db::org.At.tair.db, keys = go_keys,
                          columns = "GO", keytype = "TAIR")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(GO)) %>%
    distinct(gene = TAIR, go_id = GO)
} else {
  tibble(gene = character(), go_id = character())
}

cat(sprintf("Loci recognised by org.At.tair.db: %d of %d\n",
            length(go_keys), n_distinct(pg2gene$gene)))
cat(sprintf("Direct gene-to-term annotations: %d\n", nrow(g2go)))

# go_ok gates the chunks below, so a GO problem costs you this section and
# nothing else - the rest of the report still knits.
go_ok <- nrow(pg2gene) > 0 && nrow(g2go) > 0
if (!go_ok) cat(
  "\n!! GO section skipped. Check the counts above: if no protein group got a\n",
  "   TAIR locus, the peptide-ID mapping upstream is what needs fixing; if loci\n",
  "   were found but no annotations came back, reinstall org.At.tair.db.\n")
```

```{r go-propagate, eval = go_ok}
# Propagate each annotation up the GO hierarchy: a protein annotated to
# "response to hydrogen peroxide" also counts towards "response to oxidative
# stress". Without this, broad categories are badly under-counted.
ancestors <- c(as.list(GO.db::GOBPANCESTOR),
               as.list(GO.db::GOMFANCESTOR),
               as.list(GO.db::GOCCANCESTOR))
per_gene <- lapply(split(g2go$go_id, g2go$gene), function(ids)
  setdiff(unique(c(ids, unlist(ancestors[ids], use.names = FALSE))), c("all", NA)))

# as.character() keeps both columns character even if a list comes back empty;
# without it an empty result produces NULL columns and the lookup below fails
# with "'keys' must be a character vector".
go_prop <- tibble(gene  = toupper(as.character(rep(names(per_gene), lengths(per_gene)))),
                  go_id = as.character(unlist(per_gene, use.names = FALSE)))

go_info <- suppressMessages(
  AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db::GO.db, keys = unique(go_prop$go_id),
                        columns = c("TERM", "ONTOLOGY"), keytype = "GOID")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(TERM))

cat(sprintf("After propagation: %d genes, %d distinct GO terms\n",
            n_distinct(go_prop$gene), n_distinct(go_prop$go_id)))
```

**The test.** For each GO term: of the *B* background genes, *b* carry the
term; of the *Q* genes in the list being tested, *q* carry it. The
hypergeometric p-value asks how surprising *q* is, and fold enrichment is
`(q/Q) / (b/B)`. Terms are only tested if they cover at least 5 and at most
2000 background genes (tiny terms are noise, enormous ones are
uninformative) and if the list contributes at least 3 genes. p-values are
BH-adjusted **within each list**.

```{r go-enrichment, eval = go_ok}
# The background is the genes that are BOTH measurable here and GO-annotated.
universe   <- intersect(unique(pg2gene$gene), unique(go_prop$gene))
go_bg      <- filter(go_prop, gene %in% universe)
n_universe <- length(universe)

cat(sprintf("Genes from protein groups: %d | genes with GO: %d | background overlap: %d\n",
            n_distinct(pg2gene$gene), n_distinct(go_prop$gene), n_universe))
if (!n_universe)
  cat("!! The two ID sets do not overlap, so nothing can be tested. Examples:\n",
      "   from protein groups:",
      paste(head(unique(pg2gene$gene), 5), collapse = ", "), "\n",
      "   from Ensembl GO    :",
      paste(head(unique(go_prop$gene), 5), collapse = ", "), "\n",
      "   If those are different kinds of identifier, the locus mapping in the\n",
      "   chunk above is what needs fixing.\n")

term_sizes <- go_bg %>%
  group_by(go_id) %>% summarise(n_bg = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_bg >= 5, n_bg <= 2000)

# Hypergeometric over-representation of one gene list against that background.
# The empty case must carry the same columns as the full one: bind_rows() of
# bare tibble()s gives a table with no columns at all, and the join below then
# fails with "Join columns in `x` must be present in the data".
empty_result <- tibble(go_id = character(), n_hit = integer(), n_bg = integer(),
                       list = character(), n_query = integer(),
                       fold_enrichment = double(), pvalue = double(),
                       adj_pvalue = double())

go_test <- function(genes, label) {
  q_genes <- intersect(unique(genes), universe)
  n_query <- length(q_genes)
  if (!n_query || !nrow(term_sizes)) return(empty_result)
  go_bg %>%
    filter(gene %in% q_genes) %>%
    group_by(go_id) %>% summarise(n_hit = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    inner_join(term_sizes, by = "go_id") %>%
    filter(n_hit >= 3) %>%
    mutate(list = label, n_query = n_query,
           fold_enrichment = (n_hit / n_query) / (n_bg / n_universe),
           pvalue = phyper(n_hit - 1, n_bg, n_universe - n_bg, n_query,
                           lower.tail = FALSE),
           adj_pvalue = p.adjust(pvalue, "BH"))
}

# The whole broadened set, then split by how it behaves between treatments.
gene_of <- function(pgs) pg2gene$gene[pg2gene$Protein.Group %in% pgs]
lists <- list(
  "All interactors" = gene_of(specific$Protein.Group),
  "HL-specific"     = gene_of(pa$Protein.Group[pa$specificity == "HL-specific"]),
  "NL-specific"     = gene_of(pa$Protein.Group[pa$specificity == "NL-specific"]),
  "Both treatments" = gene_of(pa$Protein.Group[pa$specificity == "both treatments"]))

go_res <- bind_rows(lapply(names(lists), function(l) go_test(lists[[l]], l))) %>%
  left_join(go_info, by = c("go_id" = "GOID")) %>%
  select(list, go_id, term = TERM, ontology = ONTOLOGY, n_hit, n_query, n_bg,
         fold_enrichment, pvalue, adj_pvalue) %>%
  arrange(list, adj_pvalue)

write_csv(go_res, file.path(params$outdir, "YAP1C_GO_enrichment.csv"))

if (!nrow(go_res))
  cat("!! No GO term could be tested - see the diagnostics above.\n")
cat("Background genes:", n_universe, "| terms tested:", nrow(term_sizes), "\n")
cat("Genes per list:", paste(sprintf("%s = %d", names(lists),
                                     vapply(lists, function(g)
                                       length(intersect(unique(g), universe)),
                                       integer(1))), collapse = "; "), "\n")
cat(sprintf("Terms significant at adj.p < %.2g:\n", params$fdr))
print(table(list = go_res$list, significant = go_res$adj_pvalue < params$fdr))

go_res %>% filter(list == "All interactors", adj_pvalue < params$fdr) %>%
  mutate(fold_enrichment = round(fold_enrichment, 2)) %>% head(25)
```

## GO heatmap

Rows are the strongest terms (up to 8 per list, grouped by ontology);
columns are the four lists. Colour is the BH-adjusted p-value on a
`-log10` scale, **capped at 10** so a single astronomically significant
term does not flatten everything else. The number in each cell is how many
proteins from that list carry the term. A **blank** cell means the term was
not testable for that list (fewer than 3 of its proteins carry it), which
is not the same as "not enriched".

```{r go-heatmap, fig.width=9, fig.height=9, eval = go_ok}
top_terms <- go_res %>%
  filter(adj_pvalue < params$fdr) %>%
  group_by(list) %>% slice_min(adj_pvalue, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>% distinct(go_id) %>% pull(go_id)

if (!length(top_terms)) {
  cat("No GO term reached adj.p <", params$fdr, "in any list - no heatmap drawn.\n")
} else {
  hm <- go_res %>%
    filter(go_id %in% top_terms) %>%
    mutate(row_label = sprintf("[%s] %s", ontology, str_trunc(term, 55)),
           list  = factor(list, levels = names(lists)),
           score = pmin(-log10(adj_pvalue), 10))

  row_order <- hm %>%
    group_by(row_label) %>%
    summarise(ontology = first(ontology), best = min(adj_pvalue), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(ontology, best) %>% pull(row_label)

  ggplot(mutate(hm, row_label = factor(row_label, levels = rev(row_order))),
         aes(list, row_label, fill = score)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = n_hit), size = 2.8, colour = "grey15") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#fdecea", high = "#922b21",
                        name = "-log10\nadj. p") +
    labs(title = "GO terms enriched among the specific YAP1C interactors",
         subtitle = sprintf("background = %d detected proteins; cell number = proteins from that list in the term",
                            n_universe),
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
          panel.grid = element_blank())
}
```

# Files written

```{r outputs}
list.files(params$outdir, full.names = TRUE)
```

**The two lists to work from**

- `YAP1C_specific_interactors_broadened.csv` --- the specific interactor
  set (route A + route B), with a `route` column. This is what the HL vs NL
  analysis was run on.
- `YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_combined_verdict.csv` --- one row per specific
  interactor with its final HL vs NL verdict, both tests side by side.
- `YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_test_coverage.csv` --- which arm reached each protein
  (`tested_in`), with the identification and quantification counts behind
  that decision.
- `YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_untested.csv` --- the proteins neither arm could test,
  each with a `why_not_tested` explanation. May well be empty; the notebook
  says so if it is.

**Supporting tables**

- `unique_YAP1C_interactors.csv` --- route A only (absent from YAP1A).
- `YAP1C_enriched_significant.csv` --- route B only (enriched over YAP1A).
- `YAP1A_background_list.csv` --- protein groups called background.
- `YAP1C_all_interactors.csv` --- interactors before any specificity filter.
- `YAP1C_vs_YAP1A_limma.csv` --- the full probe-comparison test.
- `YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_differential.csv` --- arm 1, intensity (limma).
- `YAP1C_NL_vs_HL_presence_absence.csv` --- arm 2, detection (Fisher).
- `YAP1C_condition_exclusive.csv` --- the proteins arm 1 could not test.
- `YAP1C_GO_enrichment.csv` --- every GO term tested, per list, with
  fold enrichment and adjusted p-value.
- `uniprot_to_ensembl_peptide.csv` --- cached Ensembl ID lookup. Delete it to
  force a fresh query.
